title: Famous things and who invented them

source.name: Wikidata (CC0)
source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?invLabel WHERE { { SELECT ?item (SAMPLE(?i) AS ?inv) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?i) AS ?nC) WHERE { ?item wdt:P61 ?i . ?i wdt:P31 wd:Q5 . ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?s . FILTER(?s >= 40) MINUS { VALUES ?bad { wd:Q6256 wd:Q3624078 wd:Q82794 wd:Q486972 wd:Q9788 wd:Q33742 wd:Q3305213 wd:Q1656682 wd:Q34770 wd:Q8134 wd:Q5 wd:Q7278 wd:Q35120 } ?item wdt:P31/wdt:P279* ?bad } } GROUP BY ?item } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . FILTER(?nC = 1) OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 264

inventor.match: Match each invention to its inventor.

rows.label: HTTP cookie
rows.description: small piece of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the user's web browser
rows.hook: lets websites remember who you are by leaving a small bit of data in your browser

rows.label: regular expression
rows.description: sequence of characters that forms a search pattern
rows.hook: uses a compact pattern of symbols to find and match chunks of text

rows.label: bikini
rows.hook: is a skimpy two-piece beach outfit named after a Pacific atoll used for nuclear tests

rows.label: matryoshka doll
rows.description: Japanese-created Russian cultural icon: set of wooden dolls of decreasing size placed one inside another
rows.hook: is a set of hollow wooden figures that nest inside one another, each smaller than the last

rows.label: radar
rows.description: object detection system based on radio waves
rows.hook: bounces radio waves off distant objects to reveal their position, first used to warn ships of collisions

rows.label: dynamite
rows.hook: tamed a dangerously unstable liquid by soaking it into clay, making blasting safer for miners

rows.label: margarine
rows.description: semi-solid oily spread often used as a butter substitute
rows.hook: was developed as a cheaper spread for the army and the poor when butter ran short

rows.label: nachos
rows.hook: was whipped up at a border restaurant from tortilla chips and melted cheese for hungry guests

rows.label: coaxial cable
rows.hook: carries signals through a central wire wrapped in insulation and a metal shield, as in TV antenna lines

rows.label: gyroscope
rows.description: device for measuring or maintaining orientation and direction
rows.hook: spins a heavy wheel to keep its direction, and was used to demonstrate that the Earth rotates

rows.label: kaleidoscope
rows.description: cylinder with mirrors containing loose, colored objects such as beads or pebbles and bits of glass
rows.hook: turns bits of colored glass into endless symmetrical patterns using angled mirrors

rows.label: ballpoint pen
rows.hook: writes using a tiny rolling metal tip and quick-drying ink, and became a cheap disposable staple

rows.label: hovercraft
rows.description: vehicle capable of movement within ground effect at speed or stationary over all surfaces without contact
rows.hook: rides on a cushion of air held under a flexible skirt, crossing both water and land
